sentences.text: NOTE 14. 06.04.2026 BVLNC,J I.A.No.02 of 2025 Heard Sri A.V.Pardha Saradhi A.V., learned Legal Aid Counsel for the petitioner/appellant/convict and Sri C.Panini Somayaji, learned Additional Public Prosecutor representing the State.

Petitioner is the sole accused in POCSO Sessions Case No.80 of 2019 on the file of the learned Special Judge for Speedy Trial of Offences under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,
Nellore.

entities.text:
Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,
Nellore
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the petitioner/appellant/convict would submit that petitioner/convict was found guilty for the offence under Section 376(2)(i) of IPC and Section 5 (m) r/w 6 of POCSO Act,
2012.

Accordingly, he was convicted U/s.235(2) of Cr.P.C. and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of ten (10) years and to pay fine of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand only) in default, shall undergo simple imprisonment for a period of six (06) months for the offence under Section (Contd.) 5(m) r/w 6 of POCSO Act, 2012.
Learned counsel for the petitioner/appellant/convict would submit that the learned trial Court erroneously convicted the petitioner without appreciating the facts in proper perspective.
Hence, the petitioner preferred the appeal, challenging the judgment on various grounds.

He would further submit that the appellant already served 2  years of sentence, out of fixed sentence of ten years,
and there is a fair chance to succeed in the appeal, and there is no possibility of hearing the appeal in the near future.
Therefore, the order of sentence of imprisonment imposed by the trial Court may be suspended, pending disposal of the appeal.
Learned Additional Public Prosecutor opposed the application.
However, no written objections filed.
There is no dispute about the fact that the appellant already served 2  years sentence, out of fixed sentence of ten (10) years, and there is no possibility of hearing the appeal in the near future.

Further, considering the above facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the considered opinion that "the order of sentence of imprisonment alone imposed by the learned Special Judge for Speedy Trial of Offences under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, Nellore vide judgment dated 07.02.2024 in POCSO Sessions Case No.80 of 2019 shall be suspended, pending disposal of the appeal and the appellant shall be released on bail subject to the following conditions":
i) The petitioner/appellant/accused shall execute a personal bond for Rs.25,000/-
(Rupees Twenty Five Thousand only), with two (02) sureties for a like sum each, to the satisfaction of the learned trial Court.

sentences.text: The petitioner/appellant/accused shall pay the fine amount within four (04) weeks from the date of this order before the learned trial Court, if not paid, and file receipt before this Court.
iii) On release, the petitioner/ appellant/accused shall appear before the learned trial Court, on every fourth Saturday of the month, till disposal of the Appeal.
iv) The petitioner/appellant/accused shall not visit the street where the victim is residing in the village.
v) The petitioner/appellant/accused shall not intimidate, or try to contact or annoy the victim or her family members in any manner.
vi) The petitioner/appellant/accused shall not leave the country without permission of the Court.
vii) If the petitioner/appellant/accused violates any of the above conditions, the prosecution is at liberty to file an application seeking cancellation of the bail.
Accordingly, the application is ordered.
BVLNC,J Heard.
Admit.
List the matter in the month of June 2026 under the caption "Final Hearing".
